policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: Qere לְהַגִּיד and ketiv לגיד are both the infinitive 'to tell' (full vs. defective spelling); ASV 'to go to tell it' renders either identically and carries no mapped textual note, so the base qere fallback stands.

Qere שָׁלִשׁוֹ and ketiv שלשה both yield 'his officer/captain' (ו vs. archaic ה for the 3ms suffix); ASV 'Bidkar his captain' fits either, and the only note is alternative_rendering on 'laid this burden', which cannot decide a reading. Base qere fallback retained.
ASV 'Throw her down' renders a feminine object; qere שִׁמְטוּהָ has the 3fs suffix (Jezebel), whereas ketiv שמטהו reads with the 3ms suffix 'throw him down'. The ASV wording excludes the ketiv.

Qere וְהָיְתָה and ketiv והית are both 3fs 'shall be' (full vs. defective spelling); ASV 'the body of Jezebel shall be' renders either identically and has no mapped textual note, so the base qere fallback stands.
